harrow noun and verb

also to harrow, harrowing, hurdle

classical

Plin. NH 18.173 (Lewis & Short)
Verg. G. 1.94 (Lewis & Short)

crātis, crātis f.

noun, third declension

a hurdle of wickerwork; a harrow

Usually plural, crātēs: the wicker drag pulled over ploughed land.

Other words

  • occō, occāre, occāvī, occātum — to harrow, break the clods

    verb, first conjugation · classical · Hor. Ep. 2.2.161: segetēs (Lewis & Short)

    The noun occa, a harrow, is post-classical (Lewis & Short).

  • irpex, irpicis m. — a large rake with iron teeth, drawn like a harrow

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 10.2 (Lewis & Short); Varr. LL 5.136 (Lewis & Short)

    Also hirpex; Italian erpice.

Examples

  • vīmineāsque trahit crātēs

    and drags wicker hurdles over itVerg. G. 1.95

See also plough, rake, hoe, field.
